# External ranking evaluation (labels frozen)

This evaluation replaces opinion with history. For each task, the relevant files are the files a real commit
**modified or deleted**, and the task text is that commit's subject. The labels were therefore written by the people who did
the work at the time, not by the author of the ranker and not by looking at ranker output.

## Status of the labels

`labels.json` was generated by `select.js` and **frozen before `evaluate.js` was written or run**. The freeze is the git
commit that introduces `labels.json`; its SHA-256 is:

```text
a8205f3bb53eef6b2d96a957e43a5cd0a6d2b672d65399831e0d27c530ce69af
```

`evaluate.js` verifies this hash and refuses to run if the file differs. Labels must not be edited after seeing
results; new tasks require a new labels file with a new hash and a new, separately reported evaluation.

## Source repositories

Four public repositories of the same author as this project: `portfolio`, `alexgallery`, `lumaflow-studio` and
`premium-frontend-showcase` (URLs and the exact HEAD each was read at are in `labels.json`). They are real, independently
developed projects (Next.js/React front ends and a Laravel/PHP application) that were not written for this benchmark, but
they are **not third-party repositories**: the person who wrote the ranker also owns them. Commits may have been made with
AI assistance. Labels are the commits' changed files, whoever or whatever authored them.

## Selection rules

Mechanical and fixed in advance, documented in the header of `select.js`: newest-first walk of the first-parent history,
single-parent commits, subjects of 20 to 120 characters that are not merges, reverts, releases, dependency or lockfile
changes; 1 to 8 changed files after ignoring lockfiles, build output, snapshots and media; at least one modified or deleted
file; every third qualifying commit, at most 12 per repository. Added files are not labels (they did not exist at the parent
commit, so no ranker could return them) and are recorded separately in `addedByCommit`.

Each task is evaluated against the repository **as it was at the parent commit** (`git archive`, read-only).

## What the labels cannot tell us

- A commit's changed files are what was *changed*, not everything that was *worth reading*. A ranker that surfaces a
  helpful unchanged file is penalised.
- Commit subjects are terse ("show the title and label from the first paint"). That is realistic and also hard.
- Some commits change files ContextAnvil cannot rank at all (CSS, extension-less files, dotfiles). Those labels are kept and
  counted (`rankable: false`); the evaluation reports metrics both on rankable labels only and on all labels.
- 36 tasks over four small repositories is still a small sample, and three of the four repositories share a technology stack.

## Files

```text
select.js      label generation (rules in the header); deterministic for a given history
labels.json    frozen labels (hash above)
evaluate.js    runs one or more engines over the frozen labels and writes results
results/       recorded evaluation output
```
